title: Trait tame residue and the closed-point Gysin generator
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and let $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ be an excellent strictly henselian discrete valuation trait with $\ell$ invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Write $s,\eta$ for the closed and generic points and $i:s\hookrightarrow V$ for the inclusion. Use small etale derived categories and twists as in [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. Let $G$ be tame inertia, $A=\Lambda[[G]]$, $I=\ker(A\to\Lambda)$ and $\sigma$ a topological generator of $G$. For the constant sheaf, its supported cohomology is represented by
$$F(\Lambda)=[\Lambda\xrightarrow{1}\Lambda\xrightarrow{0}\operatorname{Hom}_A(I,\Lambda)]$$
in degrees $0,1,2$, and evaluation at $1-\sigma$ identifies the last term with $\Lambda$. Via $\Lambda(-1)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(G,\Lambda)$, the tame residue sends a character $\chi$ to the functional whose value at $1-\sigma$ is $\chi(\sigma)$. Under this model, the Gysin morphism of [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity], $\operatorname{Cl}_i:\Lambda_s(-1)[-2]\to i^!\Lambda_V$ gives the same map to the degree-two term. In particular the normalized transition of [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex] satisfies
$$\operatorname{sp}_{\eta,s}(\Lambda_V)=\operatorname{Cl}_i(1)[2]:\Lambda\longrightarrow R\Gamma_s\Lambda_V(1)[2]$$
after geometric restriction and the identity identification $R\Gamma_\eta\Lambda_V=\Lambda$. This is an equality with the Gysin normalization, including its sign, independent of $\sigma$.

source.place: Expose XVII, sections 1.2.2–1.2.3 (the exact three-term model, evaluation at 1-sigma), Definition 1.2.3.1 and Proposition 2.4.2.1(a); Expose XVI, Definition 2.3.1 for the closed-point Gysin normalization.
